ch05.card: Part 4 of 8. Asking the calculator for help.
ch05.s01.c1: This part is about the call writer, which writes a request slip, and the calculator, which answers it.
ch05.s01.c2: Rule (project rules, Oct 7): hand-written code may run only as an outside tool that the model chooses to call.
ch05.s02.c1: Code adds two numbers exactly, every time.
ch05.s02.c2: A learned network has to learn each sum from practice.
ch05.s02.c3: So the model writes its sum on a text slip (made-up numbers here) and hands it to a calculator.
ch05.s03.c1: After a round (one lap of the thinker), the call writer reads the thinker's first control vector, a list of numbers.
ch05.s03.c2: It writes one of nine choices: no call, or one of the eight operations.
ch05.s04.c1: Eight operations, with made-up numbers 12 and 5. We worked out each result by hand; ? means the call cannot run.
ch05.s05.c1: To write the 12 in a call, a learned pointer lands on its last digit, the 2.
ch05.s05.c2: The copy then steps one letter left and copies the 1.
ch05.s05.c3: A learned stop head says when to stop.
ch05.s05.c4: The copy trick was used for 98% of written operands and 91.5% of answers, on all six separate copies (T1SDR).
ch05.s05.c5: Copied here means the copy trick was used, not that the copy was right.
ch05.s06.c1: Some call numbers are in neither the question nor a reply. The call writer builds such a number one digit at a time.
ch05.s06.c2: Tested copies had 11 cells. The never-run build of the finished design has 21, last digit first; the code flips the text.
ch05.s07.c1: The calculator is ordinary Python code. It has 0 learned numbers.
ch05.s07.c2: It reads a call as text (made-up numbers here) and writes the reply as text. A call it cannot run gets a question mark.
ch05.s08.c1: In our made-up Tom example, after round 2 the call writer writes sub 12 5, and the calculator replies.
ch05.s08.c2: The reply, sub 12 5 = 7, is read as new text by the reader's letter window, which sees nearby letters, and added to the notes.
ch05.s08.c3: The question is not read again. After round 3 the call writer writes add 7 3, and the calculator replies 10.
ch05.s09.c1: In the tested design, the first call follows round 2.
ch05.s09.c2: Call k follows round k plus 1, up to call 7 after round 8.
ch05.s09.c3: The tested copies ran 8 rounds. In the built learned-stop code, rounds 9 to 32 cannot call.
ch05.s10.c1: The project owner chose any time for when a call may follow.
ch05.s10.c2: The finished design's first build lets a call follow any round from 2 to 32.
ch05.s10.c3: The tape (the list of calls and replies so far) holds 16 calls.
ch05.s10.c4: In training, 1 row in 4 gets 0, 1 or 2 extra thinking rounds before each call.
ch05.s11.c1: Some parts are still ordinary code a person wrote. Four of them are shown here in brown boxes.
ch05.s11.c2: The operation name comes from a fixed list of 8, so a new tool could not be called yet.
ch05.s11.c3: The finished design's second build writes the whole call as letters, operation name included.
ch05.s11.c4: It is built as code and has never run.
ch05.s12.c1: Each copy starts from its own random start.
ch05.s12.c2: The calculator-outside model (T1SDR) was compared with a similar calculator-inside model (B2).
ch05.s12.c3: Pooled-5 (6,040 questions kept aside), T1SDR minus B2: plus 0.62; likely range minus 0.23 to plus 1.46.
ch05.s12.c4: No copy fell over 1.0 below B2. The range includes 0: no clear difference.
ch05.s12b.c1: Chain-5, 1,000 multi-step questions: 99.6 to 99.8 with the calculator outside, mean 99.72. Inside: 99.4 to 99.7.
ch05.s12b.c2: Calculator switched off: the 2,085 questions that need it score 0.0.
ch05.s13.c1: Swap test: add and sub are secretly swapped inside the calculator. The answer should follow the new reply.
ch05.s13.c2: Pass line: 99% or more of counted rows follow the swap. Rows with two possible sources are not counted.
ch05.s13.c3: Five copies: 99.28 to 99.87, all at 99 or more.
ch05.s13.c4: The run's own first reading was 97.1 to 97.6. Its scoring rule was corrected after the misses were studied.
ch05.s13.c5: The sixth copy's saved model was lost, so it is not scored.
ch05.s14.c1: Leak check: swap in another question's thinking, then count answers still right, out of 100 (1,360 questions).
ch05.s14.c2: Limit written down before the run: 5. Five of six copies read above it, from 5.07 to 5.59.
ch05.s14.c3: B2 (calculator inside) read 3.09 to 3.75 on the same check.
ch05.s14.c4: It failed the limit. The project owner cleared it on Oct 9; it is disclosed, not a clean pass.
ch05.s14.c5: Separate reading, zero rounds of thinking: one copy read 12.94, against 10.81 for B2.
ch05.s15.c1: Tested: the calculator outside the model, at 3M, over six copies (swap check on five; leak check cleared by the owner).
ch05.s15.c2: Never run together: the borrowed Gemma reader with the outside calculator.
ch05.s15.c3: Built, never run: calls at any round.
ch05.s15.c4: Remember: the model writes calls as text. The calculator replies as text. A copy trick, with a learned stop, writes most numbers.
